title: He lied.
paragraphs:
A man chosen by God…
A man who heard the voice of heaven…
A man promised nations—
Because this isn’t just Abraham’s story.
You said you wouldn’t go back.

Same struggle.
Same weakness.
Same secret.

“You haven’t changed.”
“You’re a hypocrite.”
“God is tired of you.”
Because what happens next in Abraham’s story…
In Genesis 12, Abraham tells Sarah to say she’s his sister.
Fear of death drives him to deception.
This is not a mistake anymore.
Because sin isn’t always a moment.
And deep down you start asking:
“How can God still use me if I keep doing this?”

Genesis 20:6 (ESV):
"Then God said to him in the dream, 'Yes, I know that you have done this in the integrity of your heart, and it was I who kept you from sinning against me...'"
God still calls him a prophet.

Genesis 20:7 (ESV):
"Now then, return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, so that he will pray for you, and you shall live..."
Because your failure does not erase God’s calling—
But it does reveal your need for His grace.
Some scholars interpret Abraham’s repeated deception as a mirror of human weakness—showing that even those justified by faith still battle fear and flawed instincts.
And here’s the truth most people miss:
But He didn’t abandon Abraham either.
“Abraham messed up—and God remained faithful to His covenant anyway.”

2 Corinthians 5:21 (ESV):
"For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God."
Jesus took the weight of every repeated sin.
Every cycle you thought you’d never break.
He didn’t just die for your past sins.
So you don’t have to stay there.
Grace is not permission to stay stuck.

Romans 6:1–2 (ESV):
"Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?"
But He is also calling you higher.
You are not meant to live in cycles.
You are meant to live in surrender.
So what do you do when you’ve failed again?
Your story doesn’t end at failure.
And watch what grace does with honesty.
Pray this if you mean it:

“Jesus, I’m tired of repeating what You died to free me from.
I repent. I surrender. Change me from the inside out.”
Now don’t keep this to yourself.
Someone you know is stuck in the same cycle.
And if this stirred something deep in you…
